title: Hawaii Army National Guard Captain and Congresswoman Tulsi Gabbard reports for duty during the Puna lava flow b-roll
description: Tulsi Gabbard working in the Command Cell at Joint Task Force Response in Pahoa, Hawaii.
keywords: HIANG, Big Island, Hing, HIARNG, Pahoa, Tulsi Gabbard, Puna, lava flow, Task Force Response, Hawaii County Civil Defense, Puna lava flow, National Guard, Hawaii

transcript.text: Working here in the command ops as we have a couple of different operations going on here simultaneously,
dealing with the personnel, logistics, accountability and making sure that all the different pieces are coming together.
We have soldiers and airmen who are out on patrol as well as those who are providing assistance to the Hawaii Police Department with some traffic control points,
so making sure that we get information flow going back and forth, and also to make sure they have the support that they need to do their jobs.
Every operation needs to have a hub, needs to have a command post where information is passed through, and really where problems can be solved.
There's a lot that can happen out on the road, especially in these decentralized kinds of missions, so we need to make sure that we have real-time updates on things that are happening

both that we can feed to those who are providing assistance to, in this case the state civil defense, but also to make sure that the assistance is getting out to those who are on the ground and on the road.
I have a lot of friends who actually live in and around the Pahoa area, got some farms out here, and it's tough to be able to see the kind of uncertainty that they are facing
as we look at the lava slowly pushing its way towards the community here.
I have had a chance to spend some time here in Pahoa, both through the previous hurricanes as well as now through this threat of the lava coming through the community,
and I continue to be amazed by the optimism and really the positive attitude that people here have, even in the face of not really knowing where their future will be,
what it will be like and what their lives will be like once the lava pushes through, so it's pretty inspiring to be able to talk to and hear from them.
I love being able to serve in the National Guard as well as see how that service has enabled me to serve better as a member of Congress.
There are a lot of experiences that I continue to draw from the National Guard, my overseas deployments to the Middle East,
and even here being able to be on the ground and support this task and this mission to help the residents and the communities here in Puna.
It helps me to be able to push for different policy changes and different things on the federal level,
but also being able to come and work here on the ground with the background of serving as a member of Congress also provides a unique perspective
to make sure that both sides are working cohesively together.
As they see our National Guard troops rolling through their communities, they should know that our National Guard is made up of their neighbors,
their friends and their family people from here within our community, and they're here to provide assistance to make sure that everyone is kept safe,
to make sure the property is kept safe and to provide assistance and support in working in partnership with the local leadership here,
with the police department and with civil defense.
So these are not strangers, they're family and they're friends, and people who are excited and volunteering to be able to work to serve their community here.
